passages.text: When he had said these things, everyone remained—some for the sake of being healed, and others in order to observe those who obtained healing. Peter merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them, so that those who had been healed at once became overjoyed, while those who had observed were extraordinarily amazed and, after praising God, believed with assured hope. Together with those who had been healed, they went away to their own homes under instructions to gather early the next day. After they had left, Peter remained there with his companions, partook of food, and gave himself rest in sleep.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἱστορῆσαι τοὺς τῆς θεραπείας ἐπιτυγχάνοντας
lexical_decisions.chosen: in order to observe those who obtained healing
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἱστορέω can mean inquire into or observe closely; remaining at the scene to witness healings supports “observe.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπιθεὶς μόνον καὶ εὐξάμενος ἰάσατο
lexical_decisions.chosen: merely laid his hands on them and prayed, and he healed them
lexical_decisions.rationale: μόνον emphasizes the simplicity of Peter’s actions as the means accompanying the healing.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς μὲν παραχρῆμα θεραπευθέντας γενέσθαι περιχαρεῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: those who had been healed at once became overjoyed
lexical_decisions.rationale: The placement of παραχρῆμα within the participial phrase marks the healing as immediate, rather than the subsequent becoming overjoyed.
Treats the genitive phrase as characterizing the hope accompanying their belief; “believed in a sure hope” is possible but less natural in context.
πρωΐτερον functions adverbially of an early time on the following day.
Preserves the reflexive and the explicit reference to sleep rather than reducing the expression simply to “slept.”

source_issues.issue: The genitive βεβαίας ἐλπίδος has more than one defensible relation to πιστεύειν. The translation takes it as a genitive characterizing the manner or quality of belief; an alternative is “believed in a sure hope.” The construction remains intelligible without conjecture.
